name: WeatherFX2D
description: Add snow, rain, fog, embers, water rings and six screen distortion modes to a 2D scene. Start effects on a layer with one action; no object, behavior or per-frame update is required. Adjust intensity, wind, colour and advanced settings from events. Optional behaviors provide object-based settings and ripple placement. Effects follow the camera across the map and keep their apparent size through zoom and resolution changes.
shortDescription: Weather and screen distortion in one action. No behavior required.
author: Twillion

eventsFunctions.name: onSceneLoaded
eventsFunctions.description: Installs the WeatherFX2D runtime engine (internal).

Switching from another weather effect restores this effect's defaults. One weather effect and one distortion effect can run per layer; use separate layers to combine more effects.

eventsFunctions.name: StartWeather
eventsFunctions.sentence: Start weather on layer _PARAM1_; type: _PARAM2_; intensity: _PARAM3_
eventsFunctions.description: Start snow, rain, fog, embers or water rings with a built-in look. No object or behavior is needed. Once started it keeps running on its own - there is no "update every frame" action to remember. Calling it again on the same layer changes the running weather rather than stacking a second one.

parameters.name: Layer
parameters.description: Layer to draw the weather on (empty = base layer)

eventsFunctions.name: SetWeatherIntensity
eventsFunctions.fullName: Set weather intensity on a layer
eventsFunctions.sentence: Set weather intensity on layer _PARAM1_ to _PARAM2_
eventsFunctions.description: Change how much weather is drawn without restarting it. 0 is none, 1 is normal. Tween this to build a storm up or let it fade out.

parameters.name: Layer
parameters.description: Layer the weather is on (empty = base layer)

eventsFunctions.name: SetWeatherWind
eventsFunctions.fullName: Set weather wind on a layer
eventsFunctions.sentence: Set wind on layer _PARAM1_ to angle _PARAM2_ degrees, spread _PARAM3_
eventsFunctions.description: Change the direction the weather travels. Angles follow GDevelop: 0 is right, 90 is straight down, 270 is straight up.

parameters.name: Layer
parameters.description: Layer the weather is on (empty = base layer)

parameters.name: Angle
parameters.description: Wind angle in degrees (0 = right, 90 = down)

eventsFunctions.name: SetWeatherColor
eventsFunctions.fullName: Set weather colour on a layer
eventsFunctions.sentence: Set weather on layer _PARAM1_ to colour _PARAM2_ with opacity _PARAM3_
eventsFunctions.description: Tint the weather and set how solid it is. Opacity runs 0 to 255.

parameters.name: Layer
parameters.description: Layer the weather is on (empty = base layer)

eventsFunctions.name: SpawnWaterRing
eventsFunctions.fullName: Spawn a water ring on a layer
eventsFunctions.sentence: Spawn a water ring on layer _PARAM1_ at _PARAM2_ ; _PARAM3_ with size _PARAM4_
eventsFunctions.description: Draw one expanding ring at a point in SCENE coordinates. This is the drawn-ring kind that sits on top of the water, not the shader kind that bends the image. Needs weather started on that layer first - the Ripples type is the natural one, but any type will draw rings.

parameters.name: Layer
parameters.description: Layer the weather is on (empty = base layer)

eventsFunctions.name: StopWeather
eventsFunctions.sentence: Stop weather on layer _PARAM1_
eventsFunctions.description: Remove the weather from a layer completely and free its particles. To turn it off temporarily, set the intensity to 0 instead - that keeps the field alive so restarting is instant.

parameters.name: Layer
parameters.description: Layer the weather is on (empty = base layer)

eventsFunctions.name: StartDistortion
eventsFunctions.sentence: Start distortion on layer _PARAM1_; mode: _PARAM2_; intensity: _PARAM3_
eventsFunctions.description: Start heat haze, heat shimmer, underwater, tear lines, a magnifier band or ripples only. No object or behavior is needed. Once started it keeps running on its own. Calling it again on the same layer changes the running distortion rather than stacking a second shader.

eventsFunctions.name: SetDistortionIntensity
eventsFunctions.fullName: Set distortion intensity on a layer
eventsFunctions.sentence: Set distortion intensity on layer _PARAM1_ to _PARAM2_
eventsFunctions.description: Change how strongly the layer is bent without restarting the shader. 0 is flat, 1 is normal.

parameters.name: Layer
parameters.description: Layer the distortion is on (empty = base layer)

eventsFunctions.name: SpawnRipple
eventsFunctions.fullName: Spawn a distortion ripple on a layer
eventsFunctions.sentence: Spawn a ripple on layer _PARAM1_ at _PARAM2_ ; _PARAM3_

eventsBasedBehaviors.name: WeatherEmitter2D
eventsBasedBehaviors.description: Fills the view with weather particles that stay put in the world while the camera moves, at any position on the map and at any zoom. Attach it to any one object - the object is only a home for the settings and is never drawn as weather - then pick an Effect Type and press play. Sizes are in screen pixels and speeds in screen pixels per second, so the look holds through a zoom change.

propertyDescriptors.name: EffectType
propertyDescriptors.label: Effect type
propertyDescriptors.description: Which weather to draw. Each type carries a complete built-in look, so this alone is enough to get a good result. Ripples is the odd one out: nothing falls, and the effect is expanding rings drawn on the water - use it for a pond surface, or put it on your player and spawn rings by hand as they wade.

propertyDescriptors.name: EffectUseTypeDefaults
propertyDescriptors.label: Use built-in settings for this type
propertyDescriptors.description: ON (default): every Look, Motion, Particles and Rain setting below is ignored, and the built-in look for the chosen Effect Type is used instead - so switching Effect Type just works. Turn this OFF to author those numbers yourself. Effect layer, Enabled, Intensity and the whole Placement group always apply either way.

propertyDescriptors.name: EffectLayer
propertyDescriptors.label: Effect layer
propertyDescriptors.description: Name of the layer to draw the weather on. Leave EMPTY for the base layer. The weather is drawn inside that layer, so it scrolls, zooms and rotates with it.

propertyDescriptors.name: EffectEnabled
propertyDescriptors.label: Enabled
propertyDescriptors.description: Turn the weather off without removing the behavior. Particles are hidden, not destroyed, so switching back on is instant.

propertyDescriptors.name: EffectIntensity
propertyDescriptors.label: Intensity
propertyDescriptors.description: Multiplies how many particles are drawn. 1 = the normal amount, 0.5 = half, 0 = none. This is the setting to animate for a storm building or dying down - it works whether or not the built-in settings are in use.

propertyDescriptors.name: LookColor
propertyDescriptors.label: Colour
propertyDescriptors.description: Tint applied to every particle.

propertyDescriptors.name: LookOpacity
propertyDescriptors.label: Opacity (0-255)
propertyDescriptors.description: Overall opacity of the whole field. Individual particles also vary slightly around this.

propertyDescriptors.name: LookAdditive
propertyDescriptors.label: Additive blending
propertyDescriptors.description: Blend particles by adding light instead of covering what is behind. Right for embers, sparks and fireflies; wrong for snow, which should hide what it passes in front of.

propertyDescriptors.name: LookSoftness
propertyDescriptors.label: Softness (0-1)
propertyDescriptors.description: 0 draws a crisp square - the correct choice for pixel art, and the cheapest to draw. Raise it toward 1 for a soft round particle with a faded edge.

propertyDescriptors.name: MotionMinSpeed
propertyDescriptors.label: Minimum speed (px/s)
propertyDescriptors.description: Slowest particle, in SCREEN pixels per second.

propertyDescriptors.name: MotionMaxSpeed
propertyDescriptors.label: Maximum speed (px/s)
propertyDescriptors.description: Fastest particle, in SCREEN pixels per second.

propertyDescriptors.name: MotionWindAngle
propertyDescriptors.label: Wind angle (degrees)
propertyDescriptors.description: Direction of travel, in GDevelop angles: 0 is right, 90 is straight down, 270 is straight up.

propertyDescriptors.name: MotionWindSpread
propertyDescriptors.label: Wind spread (degrees)
propertyDescriptors.description: How far individual particles may deviate from the wind angle. 0 makes every particle travel on exactly the same line, which reads as artificial.

propertyDescriptors.name: MotionGustStrength
propertyDescriptors.label: Gust strength (0-1)
propertyDescriptors.description: Slow wandering of the wind direction over time. Two rates that do not divide into each other are mixed, so the gust never settles into an audible loop.

propertyDescriptors.name: MotionSwayAmount
propertyDescriptors.label: Sway distance (px)
propertyDescriptors.description: How far a particle drifts from side to side across its direction of travel. This is what makes snow read as snow rather than as falling dots.

propertyDescriptors.name: MotionSwaySpeed
propertyDescriptors.label: Sway speed
propertyDescriptors.description: How quickly each particle sways. Every particle gets its own slight variation on this.

propertyDescriptors.name: ParticleDensity
propertyDescriptors.label: Density (particles on screen)
propertyDescriptors.description: How many particles are visible on one screenful. The stored count is scaled up automatically to cover the off-screen margin, so this number means the same thing at any resolution or zoom.

propertyDescriptors.name: ParticleMinSize
propertyDescriptors.label: Minimum size (px)
propertyDescriptors.description: Smallest particle, in SCREEN pixels.

propertyDescriptors.name: ParticleMaxSize
propertyDescriptors.label: Maximum size (px)
propertyDescriptors.description: Largest particle, in SCREEN pixels.

propertyDescriptors.name: ParticleDepthVariation
propertyDescriptors.label: Depth variation (0-1)
propertyDescriptors.description: How strongly distant particles are made smaller, slower AND fainter together. One number driving all three is what reads as depth; varying them separately just reads as noise.

propertyDescriptors.name: PlacementAnchoring
propertyDescriptors.label: Anchoring
propertyDescriptors.description: World (default): particles hold their place on the map, so moving the camera moves past them - this is what makes weather feel part of the scene. Screen: particles hold their place on the display and travel with the camera, like a HUD overlay. Water rings and rain splashes always remain at their world positions.

propertyDescriptors.name: PlacementDrawOrder
propertyDescriptors.label: Draw order (Z order)
propertyDescriptors.description: Z order of the weather within its layer. Higher draws in front. The default of 1000 puts it in front of ordinary scene objects.

propertyDescriptors.name: PlacementPixelSnap
propertyDescriptors.label: Snap to whole pixels
propertyDescriptors.description: Round every particle to a whole screen pixel. Keeps a pixel-art game crisp, but slow particles will visibly step rather than glide.

propertyDescriptors.name: RainStreakWidth
propertyDescriptors.label: Rain streak width (px)
propertyDescriptors.description: Thickness of a raindrop. Only used when Effect Type is Rain.

propertyDescriptors.name: RainStreakLength
propertyDescriptors.label: Rain streak length (px)
propertyDescriptors.description: Length of a raindrop. Leave at 0 to derive it from each drop's own speed, so fast drops streak longer than slow ones. Only used when Effect Type is Rain.

propertyDescriptors.name: RingSpawnRate
propertyDescriptors.label: Rings per second
propertyDescriptors.description: Expanding rings seeded across the visible area each second. These are rain splashes when Effect Type is Rain, and the whole effect when it is Ripples. Set to 0 for none - you can still spawn rings on demand with the actions.
propertyDescriptors.group: Water rings & rain splashes | Custom settings

propertyDescriptors.name: RingMinRadius
propertyDescriptors.label: Ring minimum radius (px)
propertyDescriptors.description: Smallest a ring grows to before it fades out.
propertyDescriptors.group: Water rings & rain splashes | Custom settings

propertyDescriptors.name: RingMaxRadius
propertyDescriptors.label: Ring maximum radius (px)
propertyDescriptors.description: Largest a ring grows to before it fades out.
propertyDescriptors.group: Water rings & rain splashes | Custom settings

propertyDescriptors.name: RingLifetime
propertyDescriptors.label: Ring lifetime (seconds)
propertyDescriptors.description: How long a ring takes to expand and fade away.
propertyDescriptors.group: Water rings & rain splashes | Custom settings

eventsFunctions.name: SetEnabled
eventsFunctions.sentence: Set weather on _PARAM0_ enabled: _PARAM2_
eventsFunctions.description: Turn this emitter on or off. Particles are hidden rather than destroyed, so turning it back on is instant and the field does not have to refill.

eventsFunctions.name: SetIntensity
eventsFunctions.sentence: Set weather intensity of _PARAM0_ to _PARAM2_
eventsFunctions.description: Set how much weather is drawn, as a multiplier of the density. 0 is none, 1 is normal. Tween this to build a storm up or let it die away.

eventsFunctions.name: SetWind
eventsFunctions.sentence: Set wind of _PARAM0_ to angle _PARAM2_ degrees, spread _PARAM3_
eventsFunctions.description: Set the direction particles travel and how far individual particles may deviate from it. Angles follow GDevelop: 0 is right, 90 is straight down. This needs "Use built-in settings for this type" switched OFF, otherwise the built-in wind is used instead.

parameters.name: Angle
parameters.description: Wind angle in degrees (0 = right, 90 = down)

Use it as a starting point you then edit, instead of authoring 15 numbers from scratch. Runtime only - the values shown in the editor panel do not change.

eventsFunctions.name: SpawnRingAt

eventsFunctions.sentence: Spawn a water ring on _PARAM0_ at _PARAM2_ ; _PARAM3_ with size _PARAM4_
eventsFunctions.description: Draw one expanding ring at a point in SCENE coordinates - the same numbers Object.X() and CursorX() give you. The ring stays over that spot on the map while the camera moves.

eventsFunctions.description: Check whether this emitter is currently drawing.

eventsFunctions.name: ParticleCount
eventsFunctions.description: Number of particles this emitter currently holds, including the off-screen margin. Useful for checking the cost of a density setting.

eventsBasedBehaviors.name: ScreenDistortion2D
eventsBasedBehaviors.description: Bends the whole layer with a shader - rising heat shimmer, an underwater wobble, or expanding ripples you spawn where something hits the water. Attach it to any one object; the object is only a home for the settings. Strength and wavelength are in real screen pixels and stay that way regardless of what is on the layer, which is what stops the effect jumping in size as you move around the map.

propertyDescriptors.name: EffectMode
propertyDescriptors.label: Mode
propertyDescriptors.description: Heat Haze shimmers sideways in short fast waves and fades toward the top of the screen. Underwater swims slowly on both axes with a long wavelength. Heat Shimmer is the turbulent cousin of Heat Haze, built from fractal noise instead of a sine, and reads as real rising air. Tear Lines slices the screen into hard-edged strips that jump sideways, which suits pixel art and glitch effects. Magnifier Band scrolls a lens down the screen that stretches whatever passes through it. Ripples Only leaves the standing wave off entirely, so nothing moves until you spawn a ripple.

propertyDescriptors.name: EffectUseModeDefaults
propertyDescriptors.label: Use built-in settings for this mode
propertyDescriptors.description: ON (default): every Wave, Heat haze and Ripple setting below is ignored and the built-in look for the chosen Mode is used, so switching Mode just works. Turn this OFF to author the numbers yourself. Effect layer, Enabled, Intensity and Anchoring always apply either way.

propertyDescriptors.name: EffectLayer
propertyDescriptors.label: Effect layer
propertyDescriptors.description: Name of the layer to distort. Leave EMPTY for the base layer. Everything drawn on that layer is bent, including objects; anything on another layer is untouched.

propertyDescriptors.name: EffectEnabled
propertyDescriptors.label: Enabled
propertyDescriptors.description: Turn the distortion off without removing it. The shader stays attached and stops running, so switching back on costs nothing.

propertyDescriptors.name: EffectIntensity
propertyDescriptors.label: Intensity
propertyDescriptors.description: Multiplies the displacement. 0 is completely flat, 1 is the normal amount. This is the setting to tween when the player enters or leaves water.

propertyDescriptors.name: HeatRiseSpeed
propertyDescriptors.label: Heat rise speed
propertyDescriptors.description: How fast the shimmer scrolls upward. Only used in Heat Haze mode.

propertyDescriptors.name: HeatHorizonFade
propertyDescriptors.label: Fade toward top (0-1)
propertyDescriptors.description: 0 shimmers evenly over the whole screen. 1 shimmers only along the bottom and fades out completely at the top, which reads as heat coming off the ground. Only used in Heat Haze mode.

propertyDescriptors.name: PlacementWorldFollow
propertyDescriptors.label: World anchoring (0-1)
propertyDescriptors.description: 1 (default) anchors the distortion pattern to the map as the camera moves. 0 attaches it to the screen. Intermediate values give partial camera following. Spawned ripple centres always stay at their world positions.

propertyDescriptors.name: RippleStrength
propertyDescriptors.label: Ripple strength (px)
propertyDescriptors.description: How far a ripple pushes the image outward at the ring, in screen pixels.

propertyDescriptors.name: RippleSpeed
propertyDescriptors.label: Ripple expansion speed (px/s)
propertyDescriptors.description: How fast a ripple ring grows outward from where it was spawned.

propertyDescriptors.name: RippleLife
propertyDescriptors.label: Ripple lifetime (seconds)
propertyDescriptors.description: How long a ripple lasts before it has faded to nothing.

propertyDescriptors.name: RippleWidth
propertyDescriptors.label: Ripple ring thickness (px)
propertyDescriptors.description: Thickness of the moving ring. Wider is softer and more like a swell; narrower is sharper and more like a raindrop.

propertyDescriptors.name: WaveStrength
propertyDescriptors.label: Wave strength (px)
propertyDescriptors.description: Maximum displacement of the standing wave, in SCREEN pixels. This is a real pixel count and stays a real pixel count no matter what is on the layer.

propertyDescriptors.name: WaveLengthX
propertyDescriptors.label: Wavelength across (px)
propertyDescriptors.description: Distance in screen pixels between wave crests measured horizontally.

propertyDescriptors.name: WaveLengthY
propertyDescriptors.label: Wavelength down (px)
propertyDescriptors.description: Distance in screen pixels between wave crests measured vertically. Short values here make the tight horizontal banding that reads as heat. In Tear Lines mode this is the distance between tears; in Magnifier Band mode it is the distance between passes of the lens.

propertyDescriptors.name: WaveSpeed
propertyDescriptors.label: Wave speed
propertyDescriptors.description: How fast the wave animates. Each harmonic keeps its own phase, folded to one turn, so this can run for hours without drifting or popping.

propertyDescriptors.name: WaveDetail
propertyDescriptors.label: Secondary detail (0-1)
propertyDescriptors.description: Strength of a second, faster wave mixed on top so the motion does not look like one mechanical wobble. In Heat Shimmer mode this is how much each row is offset from its neighbours instead, which is what stops the noise sliding as one flat sheet.

propertyDescriptors.name: TearStrength
propertyDescriptors.label: Tear line offset (px)
propertyDescriptors.description: How far a strip jumps sideways, in screen pixels. This is a hard jump, not a gradient - the whole strip moves together. Only used in Tear Lines mode.

propertyDescriptors.name: TearWidth
propertyDescriptors.label: Tear line coverage (0-1)
propertyDescriptors.description: What fraction of each cycle is inside a tear. 0.5 means half the screen is offset at any moment; small values give occasional thin slices. Only used in Tear Lines mode.

propertyDescriptors.name: TearStripHeight
propertyDescriptors.label: Tear strip height (px)
propertyDescriptors.description: Quantises tear edges into strips this tall, so they stair-step like pixel art instead of cutting on a smooth line. Set to 0 for smooth edges. Only used in Tear Lines mode.

propertyDescriptors.name: MagnifierAmount
propertyDescriptors.label: Magnification
propertyDescriptors.description: How much the band stretches what passes through it. 1 is no change, 1.35 is a gentle bulge, 2 is a strong lens. Below 1 pinches instead. Only used in Magnifier Band mode.

propertyDescriptors.name: MagnifierBandWidth
propertyDescriptors.label: Band thickness (px)
propertyDescriptors.description: How tall the lens band is. The magnification falls off smoothly to nothing at this distance from the band centre. Only used in Magnifier Band mode.
